# Repository instructions for coding assistants

This is an introductory CTS*2000 research project, not a production app.
Read README.md, docs/project_brief.md and docs/task_board.md before editing.

- Preserve the canonical working notebook and its understandable course
  methods: loops, lists, functions, Counter, basic pandas and CSV export.
- For organization tasks, do not refactor calculations, change samples,
  replace manual coding with a classifier, or introduce new dependencies.
- Never fabricate data, citations, findings, runs, deadlines, contributions,
  GitHub handles, submissions or earlier work history.
- The supplied results are saved-output evidence, not a claimed fresh run.
  Do not mark the full-run task done without both source Excel files.
- Distinguish keyword mentions, confirmed manual complaints, per-1,000-word
  frequencies and percentages of reviews.
- Keep the unmodified analysis in Google Colab unless a runtime change is
  requested. google.colab.files does not work in ordinary local Jupyter.
- The broader proposal includes gameplay/story; do not invent completed
  analyses for them or silently decide the group's final research question.
- Extend the AI-process record and distinguish AI assistance from student
  contributions. Use actual model/time values only when known.
- Preserve existing files. Reconcile scaffold collisions carefully instead
  of overwriting unrelated work or generating competing final notebooks.
- Use issues/PRs only in the repository selected by the user. Do not send
  Slack messages, invite collaborators, publish a site or change visibility.
